# zokor API (generated by docs/gen_api.sh from src/; do not edit)
#
# `import "zokor";` then `zokor.<name>`. Methods are `value.name(..)`;
# `self` is omitted. Times are int nanoseconds, statuses i32.
# Recipes: docs/llms-small.txt.

## config.sl -- Configuration: read once, validated once, then held as a value.
gc struct Problem { key: str, reason: str, shown: str }
gc struct Config { values: map[str]str, problems: [Problem], source: str }
default_env_path() -> str
    The default file name, used by `load_config`.
load_config() -> Config
    `.env` if present, then the environment -- which always wins, so a shell override does what it looks like it does and a...
load_config_from(path: str) -> Config
    The same, from a path of your choosing (".env.test", "/etc/app/env").
get(c: Config, key: str) -> opt[str]
has_key(c: Config, key: str) -> bool
str_or(c: Config, key: str, fallback: str) -> str
int_or(c: Config, key: str, fallback: int) -> int
bool_or(c: Config, key: str, fallback: bool) -> bool
duration_or(c: Config, key: str, fallback_ns: int) -> int
    A duration in nanoseconds, the unit every slang timeout takes.
require(c: Config, key: str) -> str

require_range(c: Config, key: str, lo: int, hi: int) -> int

require_one_of(c: Config, key: str, allowed: [str]) -> str
require_duration(c: Config, key: str) -> int

require_max_len(c: Config, key: str, n: int) -> str

    An optional value that still has to be valid WHEN it is set: the common case of a feature that is off until configured.

    Same shape as optional_url, for a connection string rather than an HTTP one: `is_dsn` accepts any scheme with a host...

    Every problem, one per line, named and explained.

## errors.sl -- Failure, as one shape.
gc struct Code { name: str, status: i32, message: str }
gc struct FieldError { field: str, reason: str }
gc struct ErrorView { code: str, message: str, status: i32, request_id: str, fields: [FieldError] }
    Everything the renderer is given.
gc struct Registry { codes: map[str]Code, render: fn(ErrorView) -> http.Response }
new_registry() -> Registry
    Every HTTP failure status, under the name a handler will reach for.
set_renderer(r: Registry, f: fn(ErrorView) -> http.Response) -> int
    Replace the shape every failure is rendered in.
register(r: Registry, name: str, status: i32, message: str) -> int
lookup(r: Registry, name: str) -> opt[Code]
status_of(r: Registry, name: str) -> i32
    A code nobody registered is a bug in the service, not a client error: it answers 500 and says which name was missing, so the...
message_of(r: Registry, name: str) -> str
code_names(r: Registry) -> [str]
respond(r: Registry, code: str, request_id: str) -> http.Response
    The registered wording.
respond_with(r: Registry, code: str, detail: str, request_id: str) -> http.Response
    The registered code, with wording for this one occurrence ("no such organisation 'acme'").
respond_fields(r: Registry, code: str, fields: [FieldError], request_id: str) -> http.Response
field(name: str, reason: str) -> FieldError
default_render(v: ErrorView) -> http.Response
    zokor's own shape, and the one a service gets until it says otherwise.
quote(s: str) -> str
    A JSON string, escaped.
quote_into(sb: builder.Str, s: str) -> builder.Str
    The same, appended to a builder, which is what every renderer wants: a response is many quoted strings, and joining them here...
status_text(status: i32) -> str

## ids.sl -- Identifiers.
new_request_id() -> str
    128 bits of randomness, hex, prefixed so it is recognisable in a log that carries other people's ids too.
new_session_id() -> str
    A longer one, for a session or a socket.io sid, where a collision matters more than the length does.

Json.add_str(v: str) -> Json
Json.add_int(v: int) -> Json

    A missing key, or an index that is not there, gives Null rather than an error -- so a chain of lookups never has to be guarded...

Json.path(p: str) -> Json
    "user.address.city", "items.0.name": one call instead of five.
Json.has_key(key: str) -> bool

Json.float_or(fallback: float) -> float

    The JSON text of this value.

    Renders straight into a Bytes builder: no two-element parts list, no join, no str in between.

gc struct Checker { fields: [FieldError] }
    Decoding says a field is a string; it does not say the string is an email, or between 3 and 40 characters, or one of four words.

Checker.req_obj(j: Json, key: str) -> Json
    A nested object, so a checker can walk into it and report "address.city" rather than "address".
Checker.under(prefix: str, other: Checker) -> int
    Everything found so far, re-reported under a prefix: for a nested object checked by its own function.

## ratelimit.sl -- Rate limiting.
gc struct RateLimiter { limit: int, window: int, hits: map[str][int], lock: mutex, since_sweep: int, sweep_every: int }
new_rate_limiter(limit: int, window_ns: int) -> RateLimiter
    At most `limit` requests per client in any `window_ns` nanoseconds (1000000000 is one second).
retry_after_secs(wait_ns: int) -> int
    Whole seconds until `wait_ns` has passed, never below 1: a Retry-After of 0 invites an immediate retry that will be refused.
RateLimiter.take_at(key: str, now: int) -> int
    Counts one request for `key` at `now` (time.mono nanoseconds).
RateLimiter.take(key: str) -> int
    The same, now.
RateLimiter.tracked() -> int
    How many client keys are being tracked.
rate_limit[S](c: Ctx[S], l: RateLimiter, key: str) -> opt[http.Response]
    The body of a rate-limiting `before`: `none` to continue, or the registered `rate_limited` failure (429 unless re-registered)...

## router.sl -- The router: a request goes in, a response comes out, and the application's own state comes with it.
enum Method { GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE, CONNECT }
    The HTTP methods, as a closed set.
gc struct Ctx[S] { state: S, req: http.Request, params: opt[map[str]str], param1_name: str, param1_value: str, route: str, request_id: str, locals: opt[map[str]str], errors: Registry }

gc struct Router[S] { routes: [Route[S]], befores: [fn(Ctx[S]) -> opt[http.Response]], afters: [fn(Ctx[S], http.Response) -> http.Response], state: S, errors: Registry, auto_options: bool, auto_head: bool }
    A `before` runs ahead of the handler and may end the request by returning a response; `none` carries on.

    An application builds its router from its state alone; everything else starts empty or at the default a correct server should...

    Every method goes through here, including the ones with their own helper below, so a pattern is split exactly once and the...

    The one registration path: a pattern is split exactly once, and the rules about `:params` and `*rest` live here alone.

    The full set of HTTP methods, so no service has to fall back to `handle` with a string for anything standard.

## serve.sl -- The server edge: the accept loop that turns a Router into a running server.
gc struct ServerConfig { idle_timeout: int, header_timeout: int, body_timeout: int, write_timeout: int, max_request_bytes: int, max_requests_per_conn: int, shutdown_timeout: int }
    Four deadlines, not one, because "how long should this wait" has different honest answers depending on what a connection is...
default_server_config() -> ServerConfig
    Safe rather than infinite, per the todo item this answers.
server_config_from(cfg: Config) -> ServerConfig
    The same defaults, overridable per field from config: IDLE_TIMEOUT, READ_HEADER_TIMEOUT, READ_BODY_TIMEOUT, WRITE_TIMEOUT,...
serve_conn[S](r: Router[S], c: link, sc: ServerConfig)
    One connection, until the client goes away or asks to close.
listen_and_serve[S](r: Router[S], port: int) -> result[int, str]
    Bind, then accept until the process is asked to stop.
listen_and_serve_with[S](r: Router[S], port: int, sc: ServerConfig) -> result[int, str]
    Same, with timeouts, limits, and the shutdown drain window under the caller's control -- built from config with...

## testkit.sl -- Building a request, and reading a response.
gc struct TestRequest { method: Method, path: str, headers: map[str]str, body: bytes }
request(method: Method, path: str) -> TestRequest
get_request(path: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.header(name: str, value: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.bearer(token: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.basic(credentials: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.content_type(ct: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.body_str(body: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.body_bytes(body: bytes) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.json_body(body: str) -> TestRequest
    Sets the content type too, because a body without one is a body a real client would not send.
TestRequest.json(body: Json) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.multipart(boundary: str, fields: map[str]str, files: [Upload]) -> TestRequest
    A multipart body, built from the parts given: each file is `name:filename:content-type:content`, each field `name:value`.
TestRequest.build() -> http.Request
    Not fallible: a header that fails http.request()'s validation (CR or LF in a name or value, a colon in a name) here is a bug...
upload_part(field: str, filename: str, content_type: str, content: str) -> Upload
    One part for `multipart`, without going near a real encoder.
resp_status(r: http.Response) -> int
    `status_of` is taken by the registry, so responses read as `resp_status`, `resp_text`, `resp_header`, `resp_json`.
resp_text(r: http.Response) -> str
resp_header(r: http.Response, name: str) -> str
resp_json(r: http.Response) -> Json
    The body as JSON, or Null when it is not JSON at all -- so an assertion reads `json_of(resp).get("id")` without a guard.
resp_error_code(r: http.Response) -> str
    The error code in zokor's envelope: "not_found", "validation_failed".
resp_error_fields(r: http.Response) -> [str]
    The field names an error envelope complains about, in order, so a test asserts on the shape rather than on an exact string.

## tokens.sl -- Opaque bearer tokens.
gc struct TokenStore { subjects: map[str]str, expires: map[str]int, ttl: int, lock: mutex, since_sweep: int }
new_token_store(ttl_ns: int) -> TokenStore
    `ttl_ns` is how long a token stays valid after it is issued, in nanoseconds; 0 means until it is revoked.
new_token() -> result[str, str]
    32 random bytes as 64 lowercase hex characters.
TokenStore.issue(subject: str) -> result[str, str]
    A new token for `subject`.
TokenStore.issue_at(subject: str, now: int) -> result[str, str]
TokenStore.lookup(token: str) -> opt[str]
    The subject a live token was issued to; none for an unknown, revoked or expired token (an expired one is dropped on the way).
TokenStore.lookup_at(token: str, now: int) -> opt[str]
TokenStore.revoke(token: str) -> bool
    Ends one token (logout).
TokenStore.revoke_subject(subject: str) -> int
    Ends every token issued to `subject` ("log out everywhere", a password change).
TokenStore.count() -> int
    How many tokens are held (expired ones count until swept).
bearer_subject[S](c: Ctx[S], store: TokenStore) -> opt[str]
    The subject behind the request's `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or none when the header is missing or the token is not live.

## upload.sl -- File uploads.
gc struct UploadRules { limits: multipart.Limits, allowed_types: [str], allowed_extensions: [str], require_content_type: bool }
gc struct Upload { field: str, filename: str, raw_filename: str, content_type: str, data: bytes }
gc struct Form { values: map[str]str, files: [Upload] }
gc struct FormError { code: str, detail: str }
    The reason a form was refused: a registered error code, and a sentence naming what was wrong.
default_uploads() -> UploadRules
uploads_allowing(types: [str]) -> UploadRules
with_max_file_bytes(r: UploadRules, n: int) -> UploadRules
with_max_total_bytes(r: UploadRules, n: int) -> UploadRules
with_max_files(r: UploadRules, n: int) -> UploadRules
with_extensions(r: UploadRules, exts: [str]) -> UploadRules
parse_form(content_type: str, body: bytes, rules: UploadRules) -> result[Form, FormError]
value(f: Form, name: str) -> str
has_value(f: Form, name: str) -> bool
file(f: Form, field: str) -> opt[Upload]
    The first file posted under a field name, which is the usual case.
files_for(f: Form, field: str) -> [Upload]
    Every file under one field name: `<input multiple>` posts repeats.
total_bytes(f: Form) -> int
safe_filename(raw: str) -> str
    A client's filename, made safe to use as ONE path segment.
extension_of(filename: str) -> str
    ".png" for "a.png", lowercased; "" when there is no extension.
media_type_of(header: str) -> str
    The media type without its parameters: "image/png" from "image/png; charset=binary".

## ws.sl -- WebSocket, and Socket.IO on top of it.
gc struct WsRules { max_frame_bytes: int, max_message_bytes: int, protocols: [str] }
default_ws() -> WsRules
ws_allowing(protocols: [str]) -> WsRules
enum Incoming { Text, Binary, Ping, Pong, Close }
gc struct Message { kind: Incoming, text: str, data: bytes, code: int, reason: str }
gc struct Conn { rules: WsRules, inbox: builder.Bytes, have: int, need: int, partial: builder.Bytes, partial_op: ws.Op, fragmenting: bool, outbox: bytes, closed: bool, sid: str }
new_conn(rules: WsRules) -> Conn
is_upgrade(req: http.Request) -> bool
    Is this request asking to become a WebSocket? Cheap enough to call on every request, so a route can serve both.
upgrade(req: http.Request, rules: WsRules) -> result[http.Response, str]
    The 101 to send back, or the failure to report.
receive(c: Conn, chunk: bytes) -> result[[Message], str]
    Feeds bytes in and takes whole messages out.
pending(c: Conn) -> bytes
    Bytes the connection owes the peer (pongs, the close echo), taken out: call it after `receive` and write whatever it returns.
is_closed(c: Conn) -> bool
text_frame(s: str) -> bytes
binary_frame(b: bytes) -> bytes
ping_frame(payload: bytes) -> bytes
pong_frame(payload: bytes) -> bytes
close_frame(code: int, reason: str) -> bytes
close_because(c: Conn, why: str) -> bytes
    The close a protocol error calls for: 1002, with the reason, and the connection marked shut so nothing else is sent.
gc struct SioSettings { ping_interval_ms: int, ping_timeout_ms: int, max_payload: int }
default_sio() -> SioSettings
enum SioKind { Open, Connect, Event, Ack, Ping, Disconnect, Other }
gc struct SioEvent { kind: SioKind, namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str, ack: int }
sio_open(c: Conn, sid: str, s: SioSettings) -> bytes
    The first thing a socket.io connection needs: its session id and the keepalive timings, as a text frame.
sio_receive(c: Conn, m: Message) -> result[SioEvent, str]
    Turns one WebSocket text message into a socket.io event.
sio_connect_ok(c: Conn, namespace: str) -> bytes
    The answer to a CONNECT.
sio_connect_error(namespace: str, why: str) -> bytes
sio_emit(namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str) -> bytes
    `emit(name, args)`.
sio_emit_with_ack(namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str, id: int) -> bytes
sio_ack(namespace: str, id: int, args_json: str) -> bytes
    The reply to an event that carried an ack id.
sio_disconnect(namespace: str) -> bytes

## internal/multipart (reached as UploadRules.limits)
gc struct Limits { max_parts: int, max_files: int, max_file_bytes: int, max_field_bytes: int, max_total_bytes: int, max_headers_bytes: int, max_filename_bytes: int }
